newsitem.title: INDIA: India copper, zinc prices up sharply on speculation.
newsitem.headline: India copper, zinc prices up sharply on speculation.

text.p: Indian copper and zinc prices on Monday rose sharply while lead eased, dealers said.
Other base metals were steady in a limited activity.

Copper and zinc rose on speculative buying following reports of a price hike by local producers for June. Copper moved up by 150 rupees at 13,750 rupees per quintal while zinc rose by 100 rupees at 8,100 rupees per quintal.

"State-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd have hiked selling prices of copper by 5,000/6,000 rupees per tonne for June while privately-owned Sterlite Industries have raised copper prices by 6,000 rupees per tonne," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
He said state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd have also hiked selling prices of zinc by 1,500/2,000 rupees per tonne but kept selling prices of lead unchanged for June.

In the open market lead prices slid by 50 rupees at 4,100 rupees per quintal amid sluggish physical demand. Tin was steady at 31,200 rupees after losing 200 rupees last week while nickel was quiet at 36,600 rupees per quintal after losing 600 rupees last week.
Aluminium was steady at 7,700 rupees per quintal after gaining 100 rupees last week.
